lemmaWAS_issues: The core identity holds (repr-WAS-sec1.md l.19-22). With theta_i = y_{i-1} - y_i, tau(z) = -2^{-1} sum z_i (y_i - y_{i-1}) = 2^{-1} sum z_i theta_i. sum theta_i = 0 by cyclic telescoping (y_0 := y_k). So for z = z_P, sum z_i theta_i = sum_P theta - sum_{P^c} theta = 2 sum_P theta, and tau(z_P) = sum_{i in P} theta_i.

The equivalence with Lemma GR is exact. P -> z_P is a bijection [k]-subsets -> {+-1}^k. Also, 'Ach(z) meets tau(z) + pZ' is the same as 'tau(z) is in Ach(z) mod p = W(P)'. So 'no solution iff for all P, sum_P theta is not in W(P)' is the negation of GR's criterion. Every zero-sum theta in Z_p^k arises: y_i = y_k - theta_1 - ... - theta_i, which is consistent at i = k.

Sign sanity check: rho_1 sigma_{y1} rho_1 sigma_{y2} = rho_{y1-y2}. GR gives z = (+,-), t = 0, V = t - tau = y1 - y2, and WAS gives tau(z_{1}) = theta_1 = y2 - y1. These agree. I also re-derived Ach(z) from the C and A+- constraints, and it agrees with proof-GR.md l.51-58.

Minor statement-scope issue: the hypotheses F, R >= 1 (k >= 1) and the normalisation x = 1 (y means the normalised values) are only implicit. 'RGR word (proof-GR.md Sec. 1)' literally means length 4p-1, but WAS is applied at N = 4p-2 (INV(5) and INV(7) via N = 18, 26 in proof-DR.md l.60-63). This is legitimate because GR's proof never uses N (C_max = F - delta, E- = R - E+, size 2p; proof-GR.md l.94-96). It should still be stated in Lemma WAS.

The consequences check out: complement symmetry W(P^c) = -W(P) holds because z -> -z swaps E+ and E- and fixes Phi, delta, s0, s1. The interval telescoping tau = y_{i-1} - y_j is correct. k = 1 gives theta_1 = 0, which is consistent with GR's 'k = 1: tau = 0'. Trivial wording point: '(a set of even integers)' describes Ach(z_P), not W(P), which is a subset of Z_p.
theoremDR_issues: F = 0 and R = 0 cases (l.24-25) are correct. If R = 0, the all-reflection cyclic word is a single maximal cyclic run, so RGR forces sigma_y^{4p-1}, and any 2p of its letters multiply to 1. If F = 0, R = 4p-1 >= 3p-1, so Lemma EGZ applies (two disjoint EGZ p-sets). Optional: state the 'whole word is one run' convention in the RGR_N definition (it is implicit in proof-GR.md Sec. 4).
Existence of a run of length >= 2 (l.25-26) is correct: there are 2k runs, each of length >= 1, with odd total 4p-1.

Deletion inside a run (l.27-29) is correct. The run stays nonempty, so nothing merges and the 2k runs stay the same (same k, same x). Reflection runs stay constant, F and R stay >= 1, and subwords of w' are subwords of w, so w' is an avoider in RGR_{4p-2}(p) with F, R >= 1. INV(p) therefore applies to every such w'.
Two-long-runs contradiction (l.30-31) is correct: deleting from X gives |Y| odd, and deleting from Y gives |Y| - 1 odd.

|X| bound (l.32-33) is correct. Exactly one run X has |X| >= 2, the other 2k-1 runs have length 1, and |X| = 4p-2k. INV applied to w'_X (same k) gives k <= p, so |X| >= 2p. This is consistent with INV's parity, since |X| - 1 = 4p-2k-1 is odd.
(ii) is correct: 2p letters of the constant run X multiply to sigma_y^{2p} = 1. Wrap-around of X across the end of the linear word is harmless because all its letters are equal.

(iii): the Doubling Lemma hypotheses (proof-dihedral-partial.md l.33-39) are met exactly. It is applied to w itself, not w', so N = 4p-1, and F >= 1 holds. Since F >= 1, the maximal cyclic rotation run X is exactly one gap t_0, so j = 0 gives a stretch of 2j+1 = 1 gap and no M-gaps. Then |K| = p - 2*0 - 0 = p and the condition is sum_K x_r = 0. K = p equal letters of X (by pigeonhole on >= 2p letters in {rho_x, rho_-x}) has sum +-px = 0 mod p. This is the stated special case at l.58-59. F = 1 is also fine: M = 0 + (R - p) = 3p-2 parameters.
I found no defects. Optional: spell out the j = 0 instantiation (stretch = {gap X}, |K| = p, empty M-sum) in the text.
corollaryDRprime_issues: Setup (l.45-46): INV* applies to every one-letter deletion, because deletions of an avoider are avoiders of length 4p-2.

(a) (l.46-49) is correct. rho_0, or a pair rho_u, rho_v with v not in {u, -u}, survives the deletion of a third letter (4p-1 >= 3), and the deletion then violates the single-{+-x}, x != 0 condition (if u, v are both in {+-x} then v = +-u). So all rotation values lie in one {+-x} with x != 0, taking x to be any rotation value; this is vacuous when R = 0.

(b) (l.49-55) is correct. A non-constant maximal cyclic reflection run contains a cyclically adjacent unequal pair (i, i+1). This includes the wrap-around pair (4p-1, 1) and covers R = 0, where the run is the whole cyclic word. Deleting j not in {i, i+1} keeps the pair cyclically adjacent, both reflections, inside one maximal run of the deletion (a merge only enlarges that run). That run is non-constant, so the deletion is not RGR, contradicting INV*.
Hence w is in RGR_{4p-1}(p), and Theorem DR (under INV(p)) gives an identity 2p-subword, a contradiction. I found no issues. Optional: say explicitly that positions i, i+1 are taken cyclically.
required_fixes: Lemma WAS (repr-WAS-sec1.md l.16-18): state the hypotheses explicitly. These are k >= 1 (F, R >= 1); x normalised to 1, with y the normalised reflection values; and validity for RGR words of every length N = F + R, citing proof-GR.md Sec. 4 (GR's proof never uses N = 4p-1). The fix is needed because proof-DR.md applies WAS at N = 4p-2 for INV(5) and INV(7).
notes: I read only ./input/. I did not assess any computations (proof-DR.md 'Finite-exact status', proof-GR.md Sec. 5) or novelty. Lemma GR and the Doubling Lemma were taken as already reviewed. As sanity checks I re-derived GR's Ach(z) bounds and the sign of tau (on an explicit 4-letter product), and checked that GR's proof is independent of N; all three agree with the documents. The logical chain holds: INV(p) implies Theorem DR, and INV*(p) together with INV(p) implies Corollary DR' (no avoider of length 4p-1, hence none of any length >= 4p-1, since deleting letters keeps an avoider an avoider). All remaining open content is in the hypotheses INV and INV*. The document itself says (l.65) that neither has an all-p proof.
